claim: RawAccel's classic (legacy) sensitivity is 1 + min(accel^(p-1)*(x-offset)^p/x, cap-1) for x > offset (p = exponentClassic, x in counts/ms). For p = 2 that is a CURVE, 1 + accel*(x-offset)^2/x. AimForge had modelled it as the straight line 1 + accel*(x-offset); the two agree only at offset 0.
method: Fetched RawAccelOfficial/rawaccel master common/accel-classic.hpp verbatim: base_fn(x) = accel_raised * pow(x - args.input_offset, args.exponent_classic) / x; accel_raised = pow(args.acceleration, args.exponent_classic - 1) in cap_mode::out; LEGACY operator(): if (x <= args.input_offset) return 1; return sign * minsd(base_fn(x, accel_raised, args), cap) + 1. Independently flagged by a driver-semantics reviewer and confirmed by a second source read.
consequence: Curve.ClassicGain/ClassicCapSpeedCms implement the driver formula; EffectiveLut is now a 48-point log-spaced sample of it (error < 0.05%); Cadence Lock evaluates classic cards NATIVELY (CadenceCore.Classic*, exact to 1e-7) instead of through the 4-point linear table it shipped with on 2026-09-07 - so the pen now runs the same curve on both engines. Measurement pins re-taken. The old Cadence Lock table over-read the gain by up to 6% in the tap band for offset>0 classic cards.
fieldVerdict: pending - the user rated Cadence Lock good on the OLD (linear) table; re-test on the driver-exact curve
